verses.text: In the first month of the second year after the people of Israel came out of Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses in the Sinai desert. He said,
"The people of Israel must celebrate the Passover at its set time.
Celebrate it at its set time, at sunset on the fourteenth day of this month. Follow all its rules and laws."
So Moses told the people of Israel to celebrate the Passover.
They celebrated it in the Sinai desert at sunset on the fourteenth day of the first month. The people of Israel did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
But some men were unclean because they had touched a dead body, so they could not celebrate the Passover on that day. They came to Moses and Aaron that same day
and said, "We are unclean because we touched a dead body. But why should we be kept from bringing the LORD's offering at the set time with the other people of Israel?"
Moses answered them, "Wait here until I find out what the LORD commands about you."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the people of Israel: If any of you, or any of your descendants, are unclean because of a dead body, or are away on a long journey, you may still celebrate the LORD's Passover.
Celebrate it at sunset on the fourteenth day of the second month. Eat the lamb with bread made without yeast and with bitter herbs.
Do not leave any of it until morning, and do not break any of its bones. Follow all the rules for the Passover.

But if a man is clean and is not away on a journey, and still does not celebrate the Passover, he must be cut off from his people. He did not bring the LORD's offering at the set time, so he will carry the blame for his sin.
If a foreigner living among you wants to celebrate the LORD's Passover, he must follow its rules and laws. The same rule applies to the foreigner and to the person born in the land."
On the day the Holy Tent was set up, the cloud covered it, the Tent of the Covenant Law. From evening until morning the cloud over the Holy Tent looked like fire.
It was always like this. The cloud covered it by day, and at night it looked like fire.
Whenever the cloud lifted from above the Tent, the people of Israel set out. Wherever the cloud stopped, the people of Israel camped.
At the LORD's command the people of Israel set out, and at his command they camped. As long as the cloud stayed over the Holy Tent, they stayed in camp.
When the cloud stayed over the Holy Tent for a long time, the people of Israel obeyed the LORD and did not set out.
Sometimes the cloud was over the Holy Tent for only a few days. At the LORD's command they stayed in camp, and at his command they set out.
Sometimes the cloud stayed only from evening until morning, and when it lifted in the morning, they set out. Whether by day or by night, whenever the cloud lifted, they set out.
Whether the cloud stayed over the Holy Tent for two days, a month, or a year, the people of Israel stayed in camp and did not set out. But when it lifted, they set out.
At the LORD's command they camped, and at the LORD's command they set out. They obeyed the LORD's command, as he gave it through Moses.
